traefikConfig.title: Traefik configuration
traefikConfig.subtitle: Traefik works out of the box with no changes needed. Adjust these settings for more advanced routing setups.
traefikConfig.quickSetupHelp: Common settings, applied as Traefik command-line flags.
traefikConfig.dashboardHelp: Exposes the Traefik dashboard and publishes port 8080.
traefikConfig.dashboardAccessHint: Assign a domain and require login for the dashboard under the Access tab, instead of relying on the raw port above.
traefikConfig.exposedByDefaultHelp: When off (recommended), containers must opt in with a traefik.enable=true label to be routed.
traefikConfig.metricsHelp: Exposes Traefik metrics in Prometheus format.
traefikConfig.apiInsecureHelp: Serves the dashboard without authentication on the raw port above. Bypasses everything configured under the Access tab.
traefikConfig.apiInsecureWarning: Bypasses all authentication, including any Basic Auth configured under Access — only use this for local debugging on a port that isn't publicly reachable.
traefikConfig.accessHelp: Put the dashboard behind its own domain and require login, instead of relying on the raw port or insecure mode.
traefikConfig.basicAuthEnableHelp: Gates the dashboard's domain router with HTTP Basic Auth. Does not affect the raw port or the insecure-mode toggle in Advanced.
traefikConfig.basicAuthPasswordKeepCurrent: Leave blank to keep the current password
traefikConfig.sslHelp: Automatic HTTPS certificates via Let's Encrypt. Enable this once, then turn on TLS for individual domains.
traefikConfig.sslEnableHelp: Adds a websecure (:443) entrypoint and an ACME certificate resolver named "letsencrypt".
traefikConfig.sslReachabilityNote: Ports 80 and 443 must be reachable from the internet for the domain being issued, or certificate requests will fail.
traefikConfig.sslStagingHelp: Issues test certificates that aren't trusted by browsers. Use this while testing to avoid Let's Encrypt's production rate limits.
traefikConfig.advancedHelp: Full control over the underlying Docker configuration. The image, ports, and restart policy below apply directly; command-line flags are also editable, but the General and SSL / HTTPS tabs cover the common ones.
traefikConfig.imageChangeWarning: Changing the Traefik image or version is at your own discretion. It can lead to unexpected behavior or break routing entirely if the new version isn't compatible with this configuration.
traefikConfig.rawArgsHelp: These are the same flags the toggles above edit. Change them directly for anything not covered by General or SSL / HTTPS.
traefikConfig.saveError: Failed to save the Traefik configuration.
traefikConfig.savedNote: Saved. The sidecar will redeploy automatically if it's enabled.
